title: pvTableFFT
body:
## pvTableFFT

Computes the discrete Fourier transform of every numeric column of a table (columns whose names start with vtk are skipped; 2-component columns are treated as complex), returning a table of spectra. The sampling rate is taken from a column named Time (any capitalization, assumed evenly spaced) or else from DefaultSampleRate (ParaView default 10000 Hz), and a Frequency column is added by default. Use it for spectra of probe histories, e.g. pressure fluctuations over time from a plot-over-time table; enable UseWelchMethod for an averaged, smoother spectrum of long noisy signals.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Unevenly spaced time samples give wrong frequencies; resample the history to a constant step first.
- Without a Time column the 10000 Hz default rate is used, which is almost never the true rate; add the time column or set DefaultSampleRate.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `TableFFT`. Identity: `filters/TableFFT`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the filter. Accepted data: tables (rows and columns) (vtkTable). The input needs at least one row (table) array with 1 component. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkTable"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BlockOverlap` | Specify the number of samples which will overlap between each block / segment. If value is not in a valid range (ie inferior to 0 or superior to BlockSize) then the value BlockSize / 2 will be used. Only used if UseWelchMethod is true. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `BlockSize` | Specify the number of samples to use for each block / segment in the Welch method. This should be a power of 2 in order to achieve better performance. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `CreateFrequencyColumn` | Specify if the filter should create a frequency column based on a column named "time" (not case sensitive). An evenly-spaced time array is expected. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `DefaultSampleRate` | If the "Time" column is not found then this value will be used as the sample rate of the input. | `{"maximum":100000.0,"minimum":10.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `10.0` |
| `Detrend` | Remove trend on each segment before applying the FFT. This is a constant detrend where the mean of the signal is substracted to the signal. Only used if UseWelchMethod is true. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `Normalize` | Specify if the output should be normalized. Only used if UseWelchMethod is false. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `OneSidedSpectrum` | Specify if the filter should use the optimized discrete fourier transform for real values. This will cause output columns to have from n to ((n / 2) + 1) rows. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `ScalingMethod` | Set what scaling should be used when applying the Welch method. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Density","Spectrum"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Density"` |
| `UseWelchMethod` | Specify if filter should use the Welch / periodogram method. If true the input will be split in multiple segment to compute an average fft across all segments / blocks. This can be faster for input with lots of samples and also remove some noise. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `WindowingFunction` | Specify the windowing function to apply on the input. This allows to better process data that is not periodic. When Welch method is used, the window is applied to each frame. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Rectangular (passthrough)","Hanning","Bartlett","Sine","Blackman"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Rectangular (passthrough)"` |
